whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity was involved. Waiting too long can cost you the right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for what happened. Your compensation is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. That means your compensation isn't artificially capped just because your losses go beyond medical bills.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: We work on contingency, so you pay nothing upfront and owe no attorney fee unless we secure a recovery for you. This lets you get legal help without adding financial stress on top of everything else.

items.question: Are you a law firm?
items.answer: We handle personal injury claims directly for people hurt in Jackson and throughout Amador County. We don't charge any upfront fees and only get paid if we recover compensation for you.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to you?
items.answer: Nothing. Your initial consultation is free, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if we win or settle your case. There's no upfront cost or obligation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have two years from the date of the injury to file a personal injury claim in California. If a government entity is involved, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Jackson?
items.answer: Based on public records, reported collisions in Jackson tend to occur along corridors like Rt 49, Rt 88, and the Rt 49/88 junction, with activity often peaking on Wednesdays between 1 and 3 p.m. These are simply neutral collision counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, so being partly responsible doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your recovery would just be reduced by your percentage of fault, which our team can help you understand in more detail.
